newsitem.title: USA: Carpenter Tech to acquire Dynamet.
newsitem.headline: Carpenter Tech to acquire Dynamet.

text.p: Carpenter Technology Corp said Tuesday it plans to acquire Dynamet Inc for about $150 million in stock and cash and will assume $11 million of Dynamet debt.
Carpenter expects to complete the acquisition of the Washington, Pa., manufacturer of titanium bar, wire and powder products by March.
The Dynamet acquisition allows Carpenter to better satisfy the aerospace industry's needs for a range of technically advanced materials, the company said.
Carpenter will pay for Dynamet with 2.8 million shares of Carpenter and $51 million of cash.
Carpenter expects the purchase to have no effect on fiscal 1997 earnings per share and expects it to be accretive to earnings per share beginning in fiscal 1998.

Dynamet is currently owned by the family of P.C. Rossin, Dynamet's founder and current chairman and chief executive, and the family of Peter Stephans, the current president and chief operating officer.
After the acquisition, Rossin will join Carpenter's board. Stephans will serve as a consultant to the business.
Also after the acquisition, Stephans plans to purchase Dynamet's forged products operation in McMurray, Pa., for cash and assumption of debt, for a total of $4 million.
Robert Torcolini, currently vice president of manufacturing operations for Carpenter's steel division, will become president of Dynamet.
